instruction: From the 'Garbage Movie titles' in column B, extract only the first word of each cleaned title (after removing whitespace and applying title case) and write it to column C. Each cell in column C should contain exactly one word.

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting first word from each cleaned title. Examples: 'Minions', 'The', 'Hairy'. Agent must write 28 single-word values to column C (rows 2-29).
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Partial credit: Score = (count of valid single-word cells) / 28. Full credit (1.0) if all 28 cells contain single words.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical verification gap: Evaluator only checks that column C contains single words, but does NOT verify these are the actual first words from column B titles
Incomplete coverage: Instruction requires extracting first words FROM column B titles, but evaluator doesn't read or compare column B data at all
Logic failure: Agent could write random single words (e.g., 'Apple', 'Banana', 'Cherry') and pass evaluation, even though task requirements are not met
Missing semantic verification: No validation that the words in column C are derived from the source data in column B
No verification of cleaning requirements: Evaluator doesn't check if whitespace removal or title case formatting was applied
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Getter should read BOTH column B and column C (or modify to return both columns)
Metric should extract first word from each column B title (strip whitespace, apply title case, split, take first word)
Metric should compare extracted first words with actual column C values cell-by-cell
Only give credit when column C values match the expected first words from column B
Consider using official getters if available for multi-column reading, or create a new getter that returns both columns
